body.p: Entry of the above amendments is requested. The amendments to claim 1, 9 and 17 are supported by, for example, paragraph [0065] and Figures 7 and 8. No new matter has been added. Claims 1-29 are pending.
Claims 1 - 29 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. 2017/0164878 to Connor et al. Applicant traverses the rejections.

With respect to claim 1, Connor does not teach or suggest a non-invasive analyte sensor as claimed where each antenna in the first group and in the second group has first and second side edges that are parallel to one another, a first end and a second end; the first end and the second end of a first one of the antennas in the first group have first geometries; the first end and the second end of a second one of the antennas in the first group have second geometries that differ from the first geometries.

Connor discloses a device for non-invasive glucose monitoring. Connor discloses that the device can operate using radio waves emitted by a transmit antenna and received by a receive antenna. Figure 61 of Connor discloses an embodiment with a plurality of energy emitters 6104, 6106, 6109, 6111, 6113 and a plurality of energy receivers 6102, 6120, 6118, 6116, 6115. Paragraph [0722].
The rejection asserts that the arrangement in Figure 61 meets the previously

claimed features reciting the first group and the second group. Applicant disagrees and notes that the drawings in Connor are not described as being to scale. So any conclusions about the spacings of the antennas in Figure 61 of Connor is without merit.

Applicant also notes that Figure 61 of Connor does not teach or suggest that each antenna in the first group and in the second group has first and second side edges that are parallel to one another, a first end and a second end; the first end and the second end of a first one of the antennas in the first group have first geometries; the first end and the second end of a second one of the antennas in the first group have second geometries that differ from the first geometries. Connor is silent about such features, and is silent about end geometries of antennas within a group.
For at least these reasons, claim 1 is patentable over Connor.
With respect to claim 9, Connor does not teach or suggest an antenna array
consisting of three or four antennas, together with the other claimed features including the first group and the second group.
Figure 61 of Connor includes ten antennas. In all embodiments of Connor that

consist of just three or four antennas, the antennas are equally spaced apart. Therefore, in those embodiments, Connor does not teach or suggest a first group that is spaced from a second group with no antennas between the first group and the second group, the two antennas in the first group are spaced apart from one another a distance that is less than a distance between the first group and the second group.
For at least these reasons, claim 9 is patentable over Connor.

With respect to claim 17, Connor does not teach or suggest a non-invasive analyte sensor as claimed where each one of the antennas has first and second side edges that are parallel to one another, a first end, a second end, and a longitudinal axis; the longitudinal axes of the antennas are parallel to one another; the first end and the second end of a first one of the antennas have first geometries; the first end and the second end of a second one of the antennas have second geometries; and the first end and the second end of a third one of the antennas have third geometries; the first geometries, the second geometries, and the third geometries differ from one another, together with the other claimed features.

Figure 61 of Connor does not teach or suggest antennas having first and second side edges that are parallel to one another, a first end, a second end, and a longitudinal axis; the longitudinal axes of the antennas are parallel to one another; the first end and the second end of a first one of the antennas have first geometries; the first end and the second end of a second one of the antennas have second geometries; and the first end and the second end of a third one of the antennas have third geometries; the first geometries, the second geometries, and the third geometries differ from one another, together with the other claimed features. Connor is silent about such features, and is silent about differences in end geometries of antennas.
For at least these reasons, claim 17 is patentable over Connor.

Claims 2-8, 10-16 and 17-29 depend from claims 1, 9 and 17 respectively, and are patentable therewith for that reason alone and need not be separately distinguished at this time. Applicant does not concede the rejections to the dependent claims.
Favorable reconsideration in the form of a notice of allowance is requested. Any questions concerning this paper can be directed to the attention of the undersigned at (612) 371-5349.
